items.title: GitHub issues already fixed on master or in a release
items.body:
Hi, similar to #432 but for the GitHub issues. I went through the changes merged after 2.13 and looked for open issues that they fix. This is a limited check of the recent changes since the last release, not a review of all the open issues.

Fixed on main:

- #246 (Remove-Unused-Kernel-Packages missing from README.md): 44dada8 (#434), squashed from #247 of the same reporter, adds it to the options reference.
- #299 (difference between Remove-Unused-Dependencies and Remove-New-Unused-Dependencies): 44dada8 (#434) now explains in the README that Remove-New-Unused-Dependencies only removes the packages that became unused with this upgrade, and has no effect when Remove-Unused-Dependencies is enabled.
- #24 (mails with `MailOnlyOnError "true"` even when nothing failed): in the reported versions a run with nothing to install had `None` as result (the "Unattended upgrade returned: None" in the quoted mail), so the "only on error" check did not apply. Since 0.89 (25ff949) such a run counts as successful, and `MailOnlyOnError "true"`, read as `MailReport "only-on-error"`, sends no mail after a successful run, also with kept back packages (`test_summary_mail_only_on_error`). The other request in the comments, not getting the same mail every day for blacklisted or held packages, is covered by the new `MailReport` values `"on-new-change"` and `"on-upgrade"` from c4290e4.
- #338 (exit code 1 when a conffile prompt comes with other upgrades, 0 when it is the only one): since d81df16 (#353) a run where the only candidates are held back by a conffile prompt fails as well, so both cases exit with 1, with and without MinimalSteps.
- #377 ("failed to read deb file" for the `auxfiles` of `mirror+file:` sources): since 974ed4a (#422) the conffile check skips the fetched items that are not debs. Checked on Debian 12 with `mirror+file:` sources after `apt-get clean`: no more error.

Partially fixed on main:

- #379 (daily mail and motd notice about the blacklisted kernel packages): with `MailReport "on-new-change"` (c4290e4) the kept back packages are mailed once per version, and with `"on-upgrade"` they never trigger a mail on their own. The motd notice ("N updates could not be installed automatically") still counts them, since it reads `/var/lib/unattended-upgrades/kept-back`, which has not changed.
- #320 (download the debs in steps with MinimalSteps): since 974ed4a (#422) the install run downloads the debs of each step right before installing it and removes them afterwards. The daily `unattended-upgrade --download-only` run of apt-daily.service still downloads all of them at once.
- #345 (purge the removed packages): since 39e4a95 (#348) the auto-removals, unused kernels included, honor `APT::Get::Purge`, so with `APT::Get::Purge "true";` they are purged. The per-category options asked there are not available.

Already fixed in a released version (noticed while checking the ones above):

- #318 (Automatic-Reboot-Time not in the options reference): documented since 2.12 (94bd1f1). A comment there also asks to say that the value is passed to `shutdown -r`, which the README does not mention yet.

Superseded PR:

- #416 (typo "to chose" in the configuration templates): the same fix was folded into c4290e4, in the templates and in the test fixture, and main now has "to choose" in all of them.

items.title: Uninstalling a Debian package does not remove unused dependencies
items.body: When uninstalling a Debian package using App Center, all its (now unused) dependencies stay installed. This can be confirmed by running "sudo apt autoremove --purge" from a terminal afterwards. This issue was fixed a long time ago in Ubuntu 18.04 (see [this ticket](https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/gnome-software/+bug/1552792)) and was also working correctly in the Snap Store app (GNOME Software fork). Please, consider also supporting the autoremove functionality of PackageKit in App Center.

items.body:
Chromebrew doesn't know if a dependency is unused and there's no system to remove unused dependencies. For example, I installed `rsync`. It called a dependency `xxhash`, however when running `crew remove rsync` it doesn't uninstall `xxhash`. It would greatly increase the usability of chromebrew if this feature was added, either with automatic unused dependency removals or with something like `crew remove --unused` (`crew remove -u`). There should also be a way to indicate to chromebrew whether a package is wanted, similar to portage's `--deselect` option or apt's `apt-mark`, for example `crew mark rsync --auto` or `crew mark xxhash --manual`. Installing a package when it's already installed should also mark a package that isn't manually installed as manually installed. Maybe even showing what's manually and automatically installed would be useful, for example `crew list auto` and `crew list manual`
I'm happy to clarify what I mean if I don't make sense.

items.title: 'apt autoremove' causes havoc
items.body:
apt remove = remove just that package
apt purge = remove configuration files too
apt autoremove = remove unused dependencies too

Unfortunately, the package manage frequently has errors resulting in dependencies used by other packaged removed as well with autoremove. This can wreak havoc when a long list is shown, a user is not familiar with package names and significance and/or a user assumes the package manager protects operating system critical packages.

'apt mark manual <package>' can be used to remove it from the autoremove list. However, this begs the question whether the marked manual packages are included in Apt's 'used' definition. And whether some installation methods like from .deb files update this 'used' definition. I avoid this at all costs, and backup thoroughly before if ever used. 

FYI, edit /etc/apt/apt.conf of APT::Get::AutomaticRemove "0" and APT::Get::HideAutoRemove "1"' can disable this permanently. 

Package managers more powerful than Discover such as Muon or Synaptic can help sorting out dependencies to some extent.

items.title: APT unattended-upgrade fills disk with kernels
items.body:
New kernel packages are installed but old ones are never removed.

Consuming space is not the primary issue, but the kernel headers include a very large number of files, to the point of exhausting inodes in a smaller disk.

Try setting `Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Dependencies "true";` where automatic updates are configured.

items.title: devops(pollos): let every box patch itself at night, nothing upgrades them today
items.body:
## Why

Nothing patches the four boxes. Read over SSH on 2026-09-30 around 15:15 CEST:

| | gus | mike | walter | jesse |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| `unattended-upgrades` | not installed | not installed | not installed | not installed |
| `needrestart` | not installed | not installed | not installed | not installed |
| upgrades pending | 0 | 103 | 85 | 84 |
| uptime | 13 weeks | 13 weeks | 13 weeks | 13 weeks |
| a newer kernel is installed than the one running | yes | no | no | yes |

How that was measured: `apt list --upgradable` against package lists refreshed a few minutes earlier, so the counts are current, but gus had just been upgraded by hand (hence 0) and walter was being upgraded during the reading, so its 85 is probably already stale. The counts cover every origin on the box (Debian, Docker, Tailscale), not security fixes alone.

Two more things the reading showed:

- **A patched kernel that is never booted patches nothing.** gus and jesse carry a newer kernel on disk and still run the one from 13 weeks ago. `/run/reboot-required` says "no" on both, because the hook that writes that file ships with `unattended-upgrades`. Today nothing on a box says a reboot is due.
- **Docker has drifted**: four boxes, three versions (29.5 to 29.8), because each one got whatever was current on the day someone last ran `apt upgrade`.

## Approach: every box patches itself, there is no central job

The request was a job that walks the nodes at night and runs `apt update && apt upgrade`. The Debian answer to that is [`unattended-upgrades`](https://wiki.debian.org/UnattendedUpgrades) on each box, driven by the `apt-daily` systemd timers that are already there, and that is what this issue proposes.

Why not a scheduled CI job or an Ansible playbook pushing over SSH:

- It needs an SSH key with root on every box, held by a runner. The runners *are* two of the boxes, and every job on them gets the Docker socket, so that key would be readable by any workflow on the instance.
- The job would upgrade and reboot the machine it is running on.
- It patches nothing on a night when the forge, the runner or the tailnet is down. A local timer has no such dependency.
- "One node after another" does not need an orchestrator for four standalone boxes. A different reboot minute per box gives the same result.

The nas already runs `unattended-upgrades`, set up by hand and without automatic reboots. It should end up on the same script, the way `003-monitoring.sh` covers every host. That is a follow-up, not part of this.

## What to build

One idempotent script next to the others, `pollos/setup/006-upgrades.sh`, run once per box as root and safe to re-run. It:

1. Installs `unattended-upgrades` and `needrestart`.
2. Writes `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades`:

   ```
   APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists "1";
   APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade "1";
   APT::Periodic::AutocleanInterval "7";
   ```

3. Writes `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52unattended-upgrades-local`. The packaged `50unattended-upgrades` stays untouched, so a package update never raises a conffile prompt about it:

   ```
   Unattended-Upgrade::Origins-Pattern {
     "origin=Debian,codename=${distro_codename},label=Debian";
     "origin=Debian,codename=${distro_codename},label=Debian-Security";
     "origin=Debian,codename=${distro_codename}-security,label=Debian-Security";
     "origin=Debian,codename=${distro_codename}-updates";
     "origin=Docker";
     "origin=Tailscale,codename=${distro_codename}";
   };
   Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Kernel-Packages "true";
   Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Dependencies "true";
   Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "true";
   Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot-Time "<per box, see below>";
   Dpkg::Options { "--force-confdef"; "--force-confold"; };
   ```

4. Overrides the two timers (`systemctl edit` drop-ins) so the work lands before the nightly window instead of at Debian's default 06:00 to 07:00.
5. Sets needrestart to restart services by itself: `$nrconf{restart} = 'a';` in `/etc/needrestart/conf.d/`.

### Schedule

`monitoring.tf` already mutes every monitor daily from 04:55 to 05:20, because the router reboots in that window. Reboots go inside it, so no status-page noise and no new mute rule:

| When | What |
|-|-|
| 02:00, up to 30 min random delay | `apt-daily.timer`: refresh the lists, download |
| 03:30, up to 30 min random delay | `apt-daily-upgrade.timer`: install |
| 04:56 gus, 05:01 mike, 05:06 walter, 05:11 jesse | reboot, only when the upgrade asked for one |

walter and jesse are the two CI runners, so they never go down in the same minute. A job running at 05:00 is killed by the reboot. Accepted.

### Prompts: what a night run does where a terminal would stop and ask

Running `apt upgrade` by hand today stopped on the `apt-listchanges` pager with the NEWS of the rsync 3.5.0 security update ("press q to quit"), which lists behaviour changes. A night run meets four kinds of prompt:

| Prompt | By hand | Unattended |
|-|-|-|
| `apt-listchanges` NEWS | pager, waits for `q` (the boxes have `frontend=pager`, `which=news`) | switches to the `text` frontend under `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` and does not wait ([man page](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/apt-listchanges/apt-listchanges.1.en.html)) |
| changed conffile | asks keep / replace | **the package is held back** and stays unpatched, silently. With `--force-confdef --force-confold` it upgrades, keeps the local file and leaves the new one beside it as `.dpkg-dist` |
| debconf question | dialog | takes the default |
| needrestart "which services" | dialog | list-only unless set to `'a'`, so the old library would stay loaded until a reboot |

So nothing blocks. What is lost is the reading: a NEWS entry announcing a breaking change gets applied at 03:30 and nobody sees it. It has to land somewhere it gets read, which is the next section. `apt-listchanges` has a `log` frontend writing to `/var/log/apt/listchanges.log`; check whether the automatic switch to `text` overrides it.

For the record, that rsync NEWS does not bite here: the repo only runs plain `rsync -av` over SSH as the login user (`forgejo-runner`, `whisper`), with no rsync daemon, no `rrsync` and no symlinks owned by another user.

### Seeing that it works

The boxes have no MTA, so `Unattended-Upgrade::Mail` is not an option without adding one, and the uptime monitor is on a plan with no free slots for a heartbeat. The smallest thing that answers "is every box patched": one `make` target that SSHes into each box from the laptop and prints, per box, the pending count, whether a reboot is due, the last `unattended-upgrades` run and its result, and any NEWS since the last look. No new credential anywhere.

A push alert when a run fails is worth having, but belongs with whatever replaces the uptime monitoring.

## Decisions to make

- **Docker in the origins, or held?** Including it means the daemon restarts on an upgrade night and every container with it. [`live-restore`](https://docs.docker.com/engine/daemon/live-restore/) is off on all four, covers patch releases only, and does not apply to Swarm services, so it is no way out on gus. Many setups `apt-mark hold docker-ce` for that reason. Proposed: include it. Container-escape fixes arrive through `containerd.io` and `docker-ce`, two of the boxes run CI jobs with the Docker socket, and a restart at 03:30 costs a few seconds.
- **Automatic reboot, or only a flag?** Proposed: reboot. The reading above is what "reboot by hand when there is time" produces.

## Not covered by apt

- **cloudflared** on these boxes comes from a GitHub `.deb`, so apt never updates it. Move it to Cloudflare's apt repository in `003-monitoring.sh`, as on the nas, and add that origin. needrestart then restarts `cloudflared-health` after an upgrade, which is a manual step in `infra/README.md` today.
- **mise tools and lazydocker**: `mise.toml` gets bumped in the repo, nothing re-runs `mise install` on the boxes.
- **Container images** are already handled by the dependency PRs.
- **The next Debian release.** The patterns match on codename, so a box stays on trixie until it is upgraded by hand.

## To check while building

- needrestart in automatic mode must not restart `docker.service` on its own. If it does, exclude it with `$nrconf{override_rc}`.
- A box that boots while the router is down has to get its DHCP lease once the router is back. If it does not, move the reboots to 04:30 and widen the mute window.
- gus comes back by itself after a reboot: the Swarm services, the USB disk, the CPU governor.

## Done when

- [ ] `pollos/setup/006-upgrades.sh` exists, is covered by the shellcheck target and is listed on the microsite with the other setup scripts
- [ ] the hostname to reboot-time mapping has one runnable check in `pollos/microsite/tests`
- [ ] each box has been upgraded and rebooted once by hand, with someone watching that everything returns. They have 13 weeks of uptime, and the first reboot should not be an unattended one
- [ ] the script has run on all four, and `unattended-upgrade --dry-run --debug` lists the Docker and Tailscale origins as allowed
- [ ] the status target exists and is documented in `pollos/README.md`
- [ ] after a week: no box has upgrades pending for more than a day, and none runs a kernel older than the newest one installed

## Sources

- <https://wiki.debian.org/UnattendedUpgrades>: install, the `52…-local` override, timer overrides, needrestart
- <https://github.com/mvo5/unattended-upgrades/blob/master/data/50unattended-upgrades.Debian>: the default origins and reboot options
- <https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/apt-listchanges/apt-listchanges.1.en.html>: frontends and the non-interactive switch
- <https://docs.docker.com/engine/daemon/live-restore/>: what live-restore does and does not cover
- <https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/needrestart/needrestart.1.en.html>: restart modes

cargo-shear (または cargo-machete) で Rust の未使用依存を CI 検出 — フロントの knip と対になる供給網/ビルド時間ガード
items.body:
## 背景・課題

- フロントは `pnpm run knip`（ci.yml の frontend ジョブ）が未使用エクスポート・到達不能コードに加え「未使用依存（package.json）」を検出し、新規混入で fail する（CLAUDE.md / code-conventions.md に明記）。
- **Rust 側には未使用 crate 依存を検出する仕組みが一切無い**:
  - `src-tauri/deny.toml` の cargo-deny は `[advisories]`（RustSec）/ `[licenses]` / `[bans] multiple-versions = "warn"` のみ。未使用依存は対象外。
  - `.github/workflows/audit.yml` は pnpm audit（フロント脆弱性・可視化のみ）。
  - ワークフロー全体・`src-tauri/Cargo.toml` を見ても cargo-shear / cargo-machete / cargo-udeps / `unused_crate_dependencies` lint は不在。
  - `[dependencies]` は直接 34 本（+ target 別）。未使用依存が混入してもコンパイルは通り、cargo-deny / rust-cache / リリースビルド（lto="thin"）の対象ツリーを無駄に膨らませる。

## 提案

- `rust (deny)` ジョブ、または `audit.yml` に `cargo-shear`（または `cargo-machete`）のステップを 1 つ追加する。安定・高速（コンパイル不要、Cargo.toml と use 解析のみ）。
- 既存の未使用依存があれば初回は許可リスト/除外で green ベースライン化し、以降の新規混入を fail させる（knip のベースライン運用と同じ思想）。必須チェックに含めるか可視化のみかは運用判断（まずは pnpm audit と同じ非ブロッキング可視化でも可）。

## コスト / メリット

- コスト: **Low**（ツール 1 つのステップ追加。既存の apt / sccache セットアップ不要なレベル）
- メリット: **2**（依存ツリーの肥大抑制＝ビルド時間と供給網面積の縮小。フロント / Rust のツール対称性。効果は中規模だが恒常的）

items.title: unattended-upgrade-shutdown --wait-for-signal doesn't work
items.body:
A while ago I configured multiple Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS machines with unattended upgrade on shutdown:

```
# grep -ve '^[[:blank:]]*//' -e '^[[:blank:]]*$' /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/75upgrades-custom 
Unattended-Upgrade::Origins-Pattern {
        "site=*.ubuntu.com,n=${distro_codename}";
        "site=packages.microsoft.com,n=stable";
        "site=dl.google.com,n=stable";
};
Unattended-Upgrade::MinimalSteps "true";
Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Dependencies "true";
Unattended-Upgrade::Remove-Unused-Kernel-Packages "true";
Unattended-Upgrade::InstallOnShutdown "true";
```

After few weeks I've noticed that all of them have pending upgrades not installed. I spent some time and I think problem is with following line:

```
diff --git unattended-upgrade-shutdown unattended-upgrade-shutdown
index f59e212..8c30a53 100755
--- unattended-upgrade-shutdown
+++ unattended-upgrade-shutdown
@@ -339,7 +339,7 @@ class UnattendedUpgradesShutdown():
         res = apt_pkg.get_lock(self.options.lock_file)
         logging.debug("get_lock returned %i" % res)
         # exit here if there is no lock
-        if res > 0:
+        if res < 0:
             logging.debug("lock not taken")
             if self.lock_was_taken:
                 exit_log_result(self.signal_sent)
```

When I read documentation for `apt_pkg.get_lock()` via `pydoc3 apt_pkg.get_lock` I see:

> ```
> apt_pkg.get_lock = get_lock(...)
>     get_lock(file: str, errors: bool) -> int
>     
>     Create an empty file of the given name and lock it. If the locking
>     succeeds, return the file descriptor of the lock file. Afterwards,
>     locking the file from another process will fail and thus cause
>     get_lock() to return -1 or raise an Error (if 'errors' is True).
>     
>     From Python 2.6 on, it is recommended to use the context manager
>     provided by apt_pkg.FileLock instead using the with-statement.
> ```

So I think, per above diff, line 342 with condition `if res > 0` should be changed to `if res < 0`.

After modifying that line, I execute:

```
/usr/share/unattended-upgrades/unattended-upgrade-shutdown --wait-for-signal --debug
```

..and in other terminal I run `kill -TERM <pid-of-unattended-upgrade-shutdown>` and it works as expected now.

Review the 287 auto-removable apt packages (orphaned npm tree, image leftovers)
items.body:
## Problem

`apt-get -s autoremove` would remove **287 packages** on this host. Nobody has reviewed them. They're patch surface and disk for nothing, if nothing needs them. The risk is that a bare `apt autoremove` would take every one, dev headers included, without anyone deciding to. #319 found this while previewing the nginx purge. None of the 287 came from nginx: the count was 287 both before and after.

## What's in the set [measured 2026-10-30]

| Group | Count | How they got orphaned |
|---|---|---|
| `node-*` | 248 | On 2026-05-24 18:19 UTC, `apt install nodejs -y` replaced Ubuntu's nodejs 18.19.1 with NodeSource 24, which removed Ubuntu's `npm`. These were npm's dependency tree. `/usr/bin/node` is NodeSource v24.22.1 now. |
| `libjs-*` | 9 | Same tree, probably. |
| `gyp`, `handlebars`, `libcares2`, `libuv1-dev`, `libssl-dev` | 5 | Probably the same tree (node-gyp's build deps). **But `libssl-dev` and `libuv1-dev` are headers** (`/usr/include/openssl/ssl.h`, `/usr/include/uv.h`). A native build (a Python sdist, node-gyp) may use them now, even though no package depends on them. |
| `bridge-utils`, `dnsmasq-base`, `dns-root-data` | 3 | Probably orphaned when the image build ran `apt-get remove -y pollinate ubuntu-fan` (2026-02-18 21:50). ubuntu-fan is `rc`. docker.io doesn't need them. |
| X11, perl, desktop: `x11-utils`, `x11-xserver-utils`, `libxaw7`, `libxft2`, `libxkbfile1`, `libxxf86dga1`, `libegl1`, `libegl-mesa0`, `libgles2`, `xdg-utils`, `libnotify4`, `libnotify-bin`, `zutty`, `libfile-*-perl`, `libnet-dbus-perl`, `libx11-protocol-perl`, `libxml-twig-perl`, `libxml-xpathengine-perl`, `libtie-ixhash-perl`, `libtext-iconv-perl`, `libio-stringy-perl` | 22 | Unknown. Probably Recommends that something on the image's install list dropped. |

Nothing removes them on its own today. `apt-daily-upgrade.timer` is masked (posture `scheduled`), and `apt-config dump` sets no `Remove-Unused-Dependencies`. The only way they'd go is a bare `apt autoremove`, from a person or an agent.

## To do

1. Confirm where each group came from (`/var/log/apt/history.log*`, `aptitude why` or `apt-cache rdepends`), especially the 22 X11/perl packages.
2. Decide for each group:
   - **Remove:** `apt-get purge` of exactly the reviewed list, with `-o APT::Get::AutomaticRemove=false`. Simulate first and check nothing else goes. This is an operator-approved host change, outside the knob's quiet ranges. Record it here.
   - **Keep:** `apt-mark manual <pkg>` with a reason, so it leaves the auto-removable set. `libssl-dev` and `libuv1-dev` are the likely candidates if a build uses them. Check first: `uv sync` in a fresh worktree and `npm ci` don't fail without them (simulate, or try in a sandbox).
3. Afterwards, `apt-get -s autoremove` should list nothing, or only what was deliberately left.
4. Record the before and after counts here.

The 2026-11-08 patch window (#311) is a convenient host session, if one batch is simpler.

Found by #319.

## Architecture Finding

**Type**: tech-debt / unused dependency declarations
**Affected area**: `crates/core`, `crates/state`, `crates/math/core`, `crates/math/media`, `crates/render-core`, `crates/manim/manim-parser`, `crates/paint/paint-model`, `crates/3d/scene-3d`

Eight crates declare dependencies in `[dependencies]` that no source file in the crate references. Ten declarations in total:

| crate | `Cargo.toml` | dependency | refs in `src/` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shrimply-core` | `crates/core/Cargo.toml:9` | `num-traits` | 0 |
| `shrimply-state` | `crates/state/Cargo.toml:7` | `hashbrown` | 0 |
| `shrimply-state` | `crates/state/Cargo.toml:16` | `uuid` | 0 |
| `shrimply-math-core` | `crates/math/core/Cargo.toml:8` | `num-traits` | 0 |
| `shrimply-math-media` | `crates/math/media/Cargo.toml:9` | `num-traits` | 0 |
| `shrimply-math-media` | `crates/math/media/Cargo.toml:10` | `serde` | 0 |
| `shrimply-render-core` | `crates/render-core/Cargo.toml:12` | `serde` | 0 |
| `shrimply-manim-parser` | `crates/manim/manim-parser/Cargo.toml:10` | `serde` | 0 |
| `shrimply-paint-model` | `crates/paint/paint-model/Cargo.toml:14` | `uuid` | 0 |
| `shrimply-scene-3d` | `crates/3d/scene-3d/Cargo.toml:17` | `uuid` | 0 |

Checked per crate against every `.rs` file under that crate's `src/`, matching the crate's Rust identifier (`num_traits`, `hashbrown`, `uuid`, `serde`), so a hyphen/underscore mismatch is not the cause. `shrimply-state` is the clearest case: all four of its files (`lib.rs`, `manim_status.rs`, `player_state.rs`, `preview_focus.rs`, 503 lines total) contain no `uuid`, `Uuid`, `hashbrown`, `HashMap` or `HashSet` token at all.

The four `serde`/`uuid` rows were separately checked for derive-only use, since `#[derive(Serialize)]` needs the dependency without naming the crate. `crates/paint/paint-model` and `crates/3d/scene-3d` **do** derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize` — but they import it through `serde`, which they declare separately; their `uuid` is what is unused. `crates/math/media`, `crates/render-core` and `crates/manim/manim-parser` contain no `derive(Serialize`, `derive(Deserialize` or `#[serde(` anywhere, so their `serde` is genuinely unreferenced.

Two entries also carry feature flags that pull extra code for nothing: `uuid = { workspace = true, features = ["v4", "serde"] }` in both `paint-model` and `scene-3d`.

Note on `num-traits` specifically: `AGENTS.md` says "Use num_trait when fit." These three declarations are not that convention being honoured — they are declarations with no call site. Removing an unused line does not prevent adding the dependency back at the moment a numeric abstraction is actually written.

## Impact

- Every one of these is a compilation unit in the dependency graph of a crate that does not use it, so it is built and linked into anything depending on that crate. `shrimply-core` and `shrimply-math-core` are low in the graph, so their unused entries propagate widely.
- Unused declarations defeat the signal that a manifest gives a reader: someone touching `crates/state` reasonably concludes it keys things by `Uuid` and uses `hashbrown` maps, and neither is true.
- `cargo` does not warn about unused dependencies, so nothing surfaces these — they can only accumulate.

## Recommendation

Delete the ten lines. This is one mechanical change to eight manifests with no source edits, so it is one issue and one PR.

Verification note for whoever lands or reviews this: I could not compile it. This environment has no C linker (`cc`, `gcc` and `clang` are all absent and `apt-get` is unprivileged), so every `cargo` build fails at `error: linker \`cc\` not found` while compiling the first proc-macro build script, and `AGENTS.md` forbids building in the sandbox in any case. The table above is from reading the manifests and sources, not from `cargo check`. `make check` on a machine with a toolchain is the real confirmation — if any row is wrong, it fails loudly as an unresolved-import error rather than silently.

items.title: requirements.txt says no dependencies, but app.py needs Flask and pyserial
items.body:
**Summary**

`requirements.txt` states that no external dependencies are needed and contains only comments. `RaspberryPiWebserver/app.py` needs Flask and pyserial, so `pip install -r requirements.txt` succeeds, installs nothing, and the app then fails with ModuleNotFoundError.

**Evidence**

Third-party imports across `RaspberryPiWebserver/` and `SCPI/` (checked with grep for import statements in all `.py` files):

```
RaspberryPiWebserver/app.py:5   from flask import Flask, request, jsonify, Response, render_template
RaspberryPiWebserver/app.py:7   import serial
RaspberryPiWebserver/app.py:8   from serial.serialutil import SerialException
```

Everything else is standard library: `os, time, glob, json, threading, contextlib, subprocess, shutil` (app.py), `time, csv, threading, glob, os` (lcr_controller.py), `os, time, struct, errno` (instruments.py, both copies), `csv, time, datetime, threading, os` (instrument_gui.py). No `pyvisa` import exists in the tree (`lcr_controller.py:5` mentions it only in a docstring).

Problems in `requirements.txt`:

- Lines 1-2: "No external dependencies required!" is false. Missing: `Flask` and `pyserial` (the PyPI name; the import name is `serial`). `README.md:124` already says `pip install flask pyserial`, so the two files disagree.
- Lines 4-5: "tkinter (built into Python)". `SCPI/instrument_gui.py:12-13` imports tkinter, but on Debian and Raspberry Pi OS it ships in the separate apt package `python3-tk`, not in a venv or pip. It should be documented as a system dependency, not as built in.
- No version pins. A reference point: a development PC has Flask 3.1.0, Werkzeug 3.1.3 and pyserial 3.5; the versions on the Pi are unknown to me.
- No unused packages are listed (the file lists none), and no packages are unused in code.
- Non-Python runtime dependencies are not mentioned anywhere in the file: `gpioset` from libgpiod and one of `rpicam-vid`, `libcamera-vid`, `ffmpeg` (`app.py:97-115`).

**Impact**

A fresh venv built from `requirements.txt` cannot run the dashboard, and the failure appears only at first run. The unpinned installs can also change behavior across Flask major versions.

**Reproduce**

In a clean venv: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then `python RaspberryPiWebserver/app.py`. Expected: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flask'`. I did not run this exact sequence; the conclusion follows from the file containing only comments and the imports above.

**Suggested fix**

Replace the contents with real requirements, pinned to the versions that work on the Pi (take them from `pip freeze` in the working venv; a compatible range such as `Flask>=3.0,<4` and `pyserial>=3.5,<4` is a fallback). Move the apt packages (`python3-tk`, `gpiod`, `rpicam-apps`) into a README section, and make the README install step use `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

**Verification status**

Verified in code (imports by grep, file contents). Versions on the Pi need a bench check.

items.title: fwupd: settle the owner's hold before its 2026-11-10 review (prune recommended)
items.body:
Follow-up from #192. `fwupd` is held by the owner, declared in the knob as `exception held:fwupd 2026-11-10` (`05a4302`). This issue settles what happens by that review date.

## Background

- **The image disabled fwupd.** `fwupd.service`, `fwupd-refresh.service` and `fwupd-refresh.timer` are all `masked`, and the image deleted the conffile `/etc/update-motd.d/85-fwupd`.
- **It does nothing here.** fwupd updates device firmware, and an exe.dev guest has no firmware of its own to update.
- **It blocks unattended upgrades.** The pending `fwupd` (a 1.9 → 2.0 major bump in `-updates`) ships a changed copy of the deleted conffile. `unattended-upgrade` treats the deleted file as a conffile prompt (`Packages blacklist due to conffile prompts: ['fwupd$']`), skips the package, and exits 1. `apply.sh` refuses a bulk whose dry run failed, so this blocked the maintenance lane until the hold.
- **While held, it stays at the installed 1.9 forever.** A future security fix to fwupd, or to the libraries it pins (`libfwupd2`, plus `libfwupd3` from 2.0 on), would land in the pending set as a held finding.
- Upstream: gregoryfoster/skills#361 asks the probe to name such a blacklist itself.

## What a removal takes (read 2026-10-07, simulated only)

- `apt-get -s remove fwupd` removes **fwupd alone**; nothing installed depends on it.
- **It orphans about 57 auto-installed packages**, up from the 3 orphaned today (`bridge-utils`, `dns-root-data`, `dnsmasq-base`). They are fwupd's Depends and Recommends:
  - `libfwupd2`, `fwupd-signed`, `secureboot-db`, `sbsigntool`;
  - flashrom/gusb/jcat/xmlb;
  - the TPM2 (`tss2`) stack;
  - `udisks2` and the libblockdev family;
  - `modemmanager` with libmbim/libqmi;
  - `bolt`, `usb-modeswitch`, `tcl`.
- **All their services are idle.** `udisks2` is disabled and `bolt` is static, both inactive. `ModemManager` is **enabled** but inactive.
- **unattended-upgrade won't clean them up.** `Remove-Unused-Dependencies` is at its default (false), and `Remove-New-Unused-Dependencies` only covers packages its own run orphaned. They would sit as `apt autoremove` candidates until removed on purpose.
- **`prune-plan.sh` can't plan it.** `--component` takes only `docker postgres redis nginx ollama qdrant`, so the skill's staged prune would be done by hand (as pruning.md's "Components from outside apt" describes for installer components).

## Options

1. **Prune (recommended).** *(Order corrected 2026-10-08; see the review comment.)*
   - **Disable:** already done, since the image masked every fwupd unit on 2026-02-06. No soak is needed: the units have been off for ~8 months.
   - **Savepoint:** a tarball of `/etc/fwupd`, root-only.
   - **Release the hold, then purge, back-to-back:** `apt-mark unhold fwupd`, then `apt-get purge` of fwupd plus its 53 orphans (libfwupd2 among them), 54 packages named one by one. `apt-get -y` refuses a held package, so the hold has to go first. Doing both together keeps a bulk from hitting the conffile blacklist in between.
   - **The orphans,** purged by name from the reviewed list, never by a blanket `autoremove`. ModemManager and udisks2 are included (no modem, no TPM on this guest).
   - **Close out:** replace the `held:fwupd` line with `purged:fwupd`.
2. **Restore the conffile and let the lane take 2.0.** `apt-get install --reinstall -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confmiss fwupd`, then the next bulk upgrades it. This undoes the image's choice, brings the motd script back, and keeps a masked package updated for nothing.
3. **Keep holding,** and renew the review date. Cheapest now, but it never ends, and any fwupd security fix becomes a finding.

## Decisions needed

- [ ] Choose the option. If it's the prune, also decide:
  - the soak length (the default is 30 days from the `disabled:` line; an earlier date is the owner's call);
  - whether the orphan list includes ModemManager and udisks2.
- [ ] Optional: ask upstream (gregoryfoster/skills) for `prune-plan.sh` support for apt components beyond the six it knows. fwupd is in every exeuntu image, so other hosts will hit the same blacklist.

items.title: ops: automated + manual OS package/security updates for OCI VMs
items.body:
## Goal

Keep the OCI production and staging VMs (Ubuntu 24.04, A1.Flex) patched without manual SSH sessions. Today nothing in the repo manages OS package or security updates: cloud-init only runs on first boot (`ignore_changes = [metadata]`), so the hosts depend on whatever Ubuntu's image defaults happen to be.

## Scope

1. **Host-level daily security patches**: install a managed `unattended-upgrades` config on each VM:
   - security pockets only (plus ESM if present)
   - Docker Engine / containerd excluded, so an unattended run never restarts `dockerd` (and with it the app containers)
   - no automatic reboot, plus removal of unused kernels and dependencies
2. **Periodic maintenance workflow** (`.github/workflows/os-update.yml`, weekly schedule):
   - re-apply the unattended-upgrades config (self-healing, and also the rollout path for VMs that already exist)
   - `apt-get` full upgrade, including Docker
   - reboot only if `/var/run/reboot-required` is set
   - staging runs first; production runs only if staging comes back healthy
   - health check (`/api/v1/system/status`) after each host
   - New Relic event and Discord alert on failure
3. **Manual run** (`workflow_dispatch`) with inputs:
   - `target`: staging / production / both
   - `mode`: security / full / check (dry run that lists pending upgrades)
   - `reboot`: if-required / never / always
4. **Host script** `scripts/oci_os_update.sh` (runs over SSH via `sudo bash -s`) and a mocked regression test `scripts/test_oci_os_update.sh`, wired into CI the same way as the OCI Disk Hygiene job.
5. **Docs**: a how-to section in `docs/how_to/oci_deployment.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The scheduled workflow patches staging, then production, in a low-traffic window, and fails loudly (Discord + NR) if a host is unhealthy afterwards.
- [ ] The manual dispatch supports target, mode and reboot selection; `check` mode changes nothing.
- [ ] The script is idempotent and non-interactive (`DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`, keeps existing conffiles, waits for the apt lock).
- [ ] The unattended-upgrades config never reboots automatically and never touches Docker packages.
- [ ] CI runs the mocked script test.
- [ ] No secrets, host names or IPs are committed.

items.title: Feature Request: Track dependency origin (direct vs. transitive) for improved cleanup and resolution

labels.name: resolution: needs standard
labels.description: Should be agreed as a standard before implementation

items.body:
### What's the problem this feature will solve?

Pip treats all installed packages within an environment as first-class, user-requested dependencies. It does not retain the context of *why* a package was installed (i.e., directly by the user or as a dependency of another package). This leads to two significant problems:

1.  **Orphaned Dependencies on Uninstall:** When a user uninstalls a package, its dependencies (which may have been installed solely for that package) are left behind in the environment. This leads to environment bloat, potential for future conflicts, and a lack of a clear "source of truth" for what is intentionally installed.

    **Example Scenario:**
    ```bash
    # Environment is empty
    $ pip install "cool-library"
    # Installs: cool-library, helper-lib (dependency of cool-library)

    $ pip uninstall cool-library
    # Uninstalls: cool-library

    # Problem: 'helper-lib' remains installed, but is now an orphan.
    # There is no built-in pip command to identify and remove it.
    ```

2.  **Suboptimal Dependency Resolution:** Because pip cannot distinguish an orphaned transitive dependency from a direct one, the resolver is unnecessarily constrained on subsequent installs. It must treat every installed package as a hard requirement, which can prevent upgrades or cause installation to fail.

    **Example Scenario:**
    ```bash
    # Continuing from above, 'helper-lib==1.2.0' is installed as an orphan.
    $ pip install "data-processor"
    # 'data-processor' requires 'helper-lib>=2.0'

    # Current Behavior: The resolver sees 'helper-lib==1.2.0' as a fixed
    # requirement and fails, reporting a conflict.

    # Expected Behavior: The resolver should know 'helper-lib' is no longer
    # explicitly required and feel free to upgrade it to satisfy the new
    # dependency from 'data-processor'.
    ```


### Describe the solution you'd like

Modify pip to track the origin of each installed package. This would likely involve augmenting the installed package metadata (`.dist-info` directory).

1.  **Introduce an Origin/Requester Field:** A new metadata file (e.g., `REQUESTED_BY`) could be added during installation.
    *   For a package installed directly by a user (`pip install cool-library`), its metadata would indicate it was requested by the `user`.
    *   For a dependency (`helper-lib`), its metadata would list the package(s) that required it (e.g., `cool-library`).

2.  **Utilize this Metadata:**
    *   **`pip uninstall`:** When a package is uninstalled, pip can check for other packages that were requested by it. If a dependency is not requested by any other remaining

### Alternative Solutions

Instead of embedding metadata within each package's `.dist-info`, maintain a separate "top-level requirements" file within the environment (e.g., in `sys.prefix`).

1.  **Maintain a Top-Level List:** Pip would manage a file (e.g., `pip.toplevel.txt`) that lists only the packages directly installed by the user.
    *   `pip install <package>` adds `<package>` to this list.
    *   `pip uninstall <package>` removes `<package>` from this list.

2.  **Introduce a Cleanup Command:** A new command like `pip cleanup` or `pip autoremove` would be responsible for reconciliation.
    *   It would build a complete dependency tree starting from the packages listed in `pip.toplevel.txt`.
    *   It would then compare this tree to the full list of installed packages (`pip list`).
    *   Any package that is installed but not part of the generated dependency tree would be identified as an orphan and offered up for removal.

This approach may be less invasive than modifying the core package metadata format and clearly separates user intent from the installed state.

### Additional context

*   This functionality is standard in most other modern package managers (`npm`, `yarn`, `cargo`, `apt`, `dnf`), where the concept of removing unused dependencies is a core feature.
*   The strong user demand for this is evident from the existence and popularity of third-party tools like `pip-autoremove` and `pip-deptree`, which were created specifically to fill this gap in pip's functionality.
*   Implementing this would significantly improve the user experience, lead to cleaner and more predictable environments, and make the dependency resolver more robust and intelligent.

# 使用 Docker 部署 Node 应用 - 镜像文件尺寸的优化

前面 [使用 Docker 部署 Node 应用](https://github.com/wayou/wayou.github.io/issues/281) 一文中完成了镜像的创建和运行，不过生成的镜像还有些粗糙，需要进一步优化。

## 镜像的优化

通过 `docker images` 看到简单的一个 node 服务端应用，超过 1G 大小，因此需要优化一下使其更加轻量。

通过如下命令查看镜像文件里都有什么文件以及分别占用的空间大小：

```sh
$ docker history --human --format "{{.CreatedBy}}: {{.Size}}" wayou/my-app 
CMD ["node" "dist/main"]: 0B
EXPOSE map[3000/tcp:{}]: 0B
COPY . . # buildkit: 2.24MB
RUN /bin/sh -c yarn build # buildkit: 118B
RUN /bin/sh -c yarn install --frozen-lockfil…: 484MB
RUN /bin/sh -c curl -o- -L https://yarnpkg.c…: 7.59MB
COPY package.json yarn.lock ./ # buildkit: 271kB
WORKDIR /usr/src/app: 0B
/bin/sh -c #(nop)  CMD ["node"]: 0B
/bin/sh -c #(nop)  ENTRYPOINT ["docker-entry…: 0B
/bin/sh -c #(nop) COPY file:238737301d473041…: 116B
/bin/sh -c set -ex   && for key in     6A010…: 7.76MB
/bin/sh -c #(nop)  ENV YARN_VERSION=1.22.5: 0B
/bin/sh -c ARCH= && dpkgArch="$(dpkg --print…: 100MB
/bin/sh -c #(nop)  ENV NODE_VERSION=14.17.0: 0B
/bin/sh -c groupadd --gid 1000 node   && use…: 333kB
/bin/sh -c set -ex;  apt-get update;  apt-ge…: 561MB
/bin/sh -c apt-get update && apt-get install…: 141MB
/bin/sh -c set -ex;  if ! command -v gpg > /…: 7.82MB
/bin/sh -c set -eux;  apt-get update;  apt-g…: 24.1MB
/bin/sh -c #(nop)  CMD ["bash"]: 0B
/bin/sh -c #(nop) ADD file:d9e4f6f4fc33703b7…: 101MB
```

### 使用更小的基础镜像

通过 [node 在 Docker 市场的界面](https://hub.docker.com/_/node/)可看到，其中包含很多可使用的选择，

- jessie-*
- buster-*
- stretch-*
- alpine-*

其中 jessie-*, buster-* and stretch-* 基于 Debian 系统，alpine-* 则是 Alpine Linux。一般使用 alpine 即可。

```diff
- FROM node:14
+ FROM node:14-alpine
```

再次查看大小，减少了一半多来到 600+M

```sh
$ docker images
REPOSITORY            TAG       IMAGE ID       CREATED          SIZE
wayou/my-app   latest    f8b6ba45c68f   21 seconds ago   603MB
<none>                <none>    fe1ff8163c15   23 hours ago     1.44GB
<none>                <none>    6e0fb94473a1   3 days ago       1.44GB
```

### 多次编译

详情及原理参见 [Use multi-stage builds](https://docs.docker.com/develop/develop-images/multistage-build/)。简单来说，构建镜像文件包含很多步骤，中间步骤依赖使用的东西其实在最后成品中并不需要。

因此，我们可以将整个构建过程分成多步，得到一些中间结果。而这些中间结果是下一步所需要的，但生成这些中间结果的依赖却是下一步不需要的，就可以舍弃。

优化后的 Dockerfile:

```
######## step 1 ########
FROM node:14-alpine AS BUILD_IMAGE

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app


# Install app dependencies
# A wildcard is used to ensure both package.json AND package-lock.json are copied
# where available (npm@5+)
# this is for npm
# COPY package*.json ./
# but we use yarn
COPY ["package.json", "yarn.lock", "./"]

# npm comes with node
# RUN npm install
# if we use yarn, we need firstly install it
# RUN curl -o- -L https://yarnpkg.com/install.sh | bash

# equivalent for `npm ci`, see https://stackoverflow.com/a/58525708/1553656
# If you are building your code for production
# RUN npm ci --only=production
RUN yarn install --frozen-lockfile

# Bundle app source
COPY . .

RUN yarn build

######## step 2 ########

FROM node:14-alpine

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

COPY --from=BUILD_IMAGE /usr/src/app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=BUILD_IMAGE /usr/src/app/node_modules ./node_modules

EXPOSE 3000
CMD [ "node", "dist/main" ]
```

再次生成镜像后查看大小，又减小了一半，来到 300+M，

```
$  docker images
REPOSITORY            TAG       IMAGE ID       CREATED          SIZE
wayou/my-app   latest    c0ffda4c908a   19 seconds ago   351MB
<none>                <none>    f8b6ba45c68f   18 minutes ago   603MB
<none>                <none>    fe1ff8163c15   23 hours ago     1.44GB
```


### 优化 node 依赖

去掉 `devDependency`，更新安装的命令：

```diff
- RUN yarn install --frozen-lockfile
+ RUN yarn install --frozen-lockfile --production=true
```

但是，如果编译过程需要编译 TypeScript，跑测试，跑 Lint 等，此方法就不适用，因为这些依赖均在 `devDependency`。

凡事无绝对，虽然安装时不能去掉，但可以在用完之后去掉。

所以在 `yarn build` 之后使用 `npm prune` 来手动删除这些无用的依赖：

```diff

RUN yarn build

+ # remove development dependencies
+ RUN npm prune --production
```
再次查看大小，减小了一半多：

```
$ docker images
REPOSITORY            TAG       IMAGE ID       CREATED          SIZE
wayou/my-app   latest    9aba2a428703   5 seconds ago    129MB
<none>                <none>    c0ffda4c908a   11 minutes ago   351MB
<none>                <none>    f8b6ba45c68f   29 minutes ago   603MB
<none>                <none>    fe1ff8163c15   23 hours ago     1.44GB
<none>                <none>    6e0fb94473a1   3 days ago       1.44GB
```

### node-prune

使用 [node-prune](https://github.com/tj/node-prune) 进一步删除依赖中的无用文件，比如 markdown，测试文件，TypeScript 的类型文件等。

更新后的 Dockerfile:

```
FROM node:14-alpine AS BUILD_IMAGE

# install node-prune (https://github.com/tj/node-prune)
RUN curl -sf https://gobinaries.com/tj/node-prune | sh

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app
…

RUN yarn build

# remove development dependencies
RUN npm prune --production

# run node prune
RUN /usr/local/bin/node-prune

FROM node:14-alpine

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

…
```

注意，运行上面的 Dockerfile 后会报如下错误：

```sh
 => ERROR [build_image 2/9] RUN curl -sfL https://install.goreleaser.com/github.com/tj/node-prune.sh | bash              0.4s
------
 > [build_image 2/9] RUN curl -sfL https://install.goreleaser.com/github.com/tj/node-prune.sh | bash:
#6 0.366 /bin/sh: curl: not found
#6 0.366 /bin/sh: bash: not found
```

那是因为切换到 `node:12-alpine` 镜像后其中不再包含 curl 命令，需要单独安装下：

```
FROM node:14-alpine AS BUILD_IMAGE

# alpine doesn't come with curl
RUN apk update && apk add curl bash && rm -rf /var/cache/apk/*

# install node-prune (https://github.com/tj/node-prune)
RUN curl -sfL https://install.goreleaser.com/github.com/tj/node-prune.sh | bash -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

…
```

这次优化后的大小减少了几 M:

```sh
$ docker images
REPOSITORY            TAG       IMAGE ID       CREATED             SIZE
wayou/my-app   latest    113ca4503190   3 minutes ago       126MB
<none>                <none>    9aba2a428703   46 minutes ago      129MB
<none>                <none>    c0ffda4c908a   57 minutes ago      351MB
<none>                <none>    f8b6ba45c68f   About an hour ago   603MB
<none>                <none>    fe1ff8163c15   24 hours ago        1.44GB
```

## 手动删除

根据 [Honey, I shrunk the node_modules! ...and improved app’s performance in the process](https://tsh.io/blog/reduce-node-modules-for-better-performance/) 里的介绍再手动删除一些依赖文件：


```
…
# run node prune
RUN /usr/local/bin/node-prune


# remove unused dependencies
RUN rm -rf node_modules/rxjs/src/
RUN rm -rf node_modules/rxjs/bundles/
RUN rm -rf node_modules/rxjs/_esm5/
RUN rm -rf node_modules/rxjs/_esm2015/


FROM node:14-alpine
…

```

查看大小，减小了 3M，聊胜于无：

```sh
$ docker images
REPOSITORY            TAG       IMAGE ID       CREATED             SIZE
wayou/my-app   latest    2c54b4ee27cd   4 seconds ago       123MB
<none>                <none>    113ca4503190   9 minutes ago       126MB
<none>                <none>    9aba2a428703   52 minutes ago      129MB
<none>                <none>    c0ffda4c908a   About an hour ago   351MB
<none>                <none>    f8b6ba45c68f   About an hour ago   603MB
<none>                <none>    fe1ff8163c15   24 hours ago        1.44GB
<none>                <none>    6e0fb94473a1   3 days ago          1.44GB
```

## 相关资源

- [Use multi-stage builds](https://docs.docker.com/develop/develop-images/multistage-build/)
- [How We Reduce Node Docker Image Size In 3 Steps](https://medium.com/trendyol-tech/how-we-reduce-node-docker-image-size-in-3-steps-ff2762b51d5a)

items.body:
# Add moosicbox_file_watcher package for cross-platform file monitoring

## Overview

Add a new Rust package `moosicbox_file_watcher` that provides a cross-platform CLI tool for monitoring filesystem changes. This will be used in GitHub Actions workflows to watch the Claude stream file, enabling real-time comment updates.

### Benefits

- ✅ **Cross-platform** - Works on Linux, macOS, Windows (useful for local workflow testing)
- ✅ **Fast CI builds** - Rust binary can be cached, no system package installation needed
- ✅ **Type-safe** - Leverages Rust's type system and error handling
- ✅ **Maintainable** - Rust code in our repo, consistent with project standards
- ✅ **Cacheable** - Binary can be cached via `cache-artifact` action
- ✅ **Portable** - Single binary with no external dependencies

## Use Case

The file watcher will monitor the Claude stream JSONL file for modifications, allowing `stream-watcher.sh` to process new events and update GitHub comments in real-time during Claude workflow execution.

**Current approach:**
- Uses `inotify-tools` (Linux-only system package)
- Requires `apt-get install -y inotify-tools` in workflows

**New approach:**
- Pure Rust implementation using the `notify` crate
- Built and cached as part of CI workflow
- Drop-in compatible CLI interface

## License Compatibility

✅ The `notify` crate uses CC0-1.0 (Creative Commons Zero - Public Domain), which is already approved in `deny.toml:97` and is compatible with MoosicBox's MPL-2.0 license.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Create Package Structure

```
packages/file_watcher/
├── .cargo/
│   └── config.toml          # Standard workspace cargo config
├── src/
│   ├── main.rs              # CLI binary implementation
│   └── lib.rs               # Core library (minimal, no CLI deps)
├── Cargo.toml
└── README.md
```

### 2. Package Configuration

**Cargo.toml:**
```toml
[package]
name = "moosicbox_file_watcher"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[[bin]]
name = "moosicbox-file-watcher"
path = "src/main.rs"
required-features = ["cli"]

[dependencies]
moosicbox_logging = { workspace = true }
notify = { workspace = true }
# CLI-only dependencies (optional)
clap = { workspace = true, features = ["derive"], optional = true }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["rt", "signal"], optional = true }

[features]
default = []

# Enable CLI binary with argument parsing
cli = ["dep:clap", "dep:tokio"]

fail-on-warnings = []
```

**Important:** CLI-only dependencies (`clap`, `tokio`) should be marked as `optional = true` and only enabled via the `cli` feature. This follows the pattern used in `packages/openport/Cargo.toml:19-31`, keeping the library lean for potential future library usage.

**.cargo/config.toml:**
```toml
[build]
rustflags = ["--cfg", "tokio_unstable"]
```

**Clippy directives in src/main.rs:**
```rust
#![cfg_attr(feature = "fail-on-warnings", deny(warnings))]
#![warn(clippy::all, clippy::pedantic, clippy::nursery, clippy::cargo)]
#![allow(clippy::multiple_crate_versions)]
```

**Clippy directives in src/lib.rs:**
```rust
#![cfg_attr(feature = "fail-on-warnings", deny(warnings))]
#![warn(clippy::all, clippy::pedantic, clippy::nursery, clippy::cargo)]
#![allow(clippy::multiple_crate_versions)]
```

### 3. CLI Interface

**Design for compatibility with existing shell scripts:**
```bash
moosicbox-file-watcher -q -m -e modify,close_write "$stream_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
```

**CLI Arguments:**
```
moosicbox-file-watcher [OPTIONS] <PATH>

OPTIONS:
  -q, --quiet              Quiet mode (suppress event output)
  -m, --monitor           Monitor continuously (vs one-shot)
  -e, --events <EVENTS>   Comma-separated events to watch (modify,close_write,create,remove,etc)
  -h, --help              Print help
  -V, --version           Print version

ARGS:
  <PATH>  Directory or file to watch
```

### 4. Implementation Details

**Core Features:**
- Use `notify::RecommendedWatcher` for cross-platform filesystem watching
- Use `clap` for CLI argument parsing (already in workspace, CLI-only optional dependency)
- Use `tokio` for async runtime and signal handling (CLI-only optional dependency)
- Handle signals (`SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`) for graceful shutdown
- Quiet mode support (no output when `-q` is specified)
- Background execution compatible (via shell `&`)
- Follow MoosicBox code style guidelines (see AGENTS.md)

**Library Structure:**
- `src/lib.rs` - Core file watching logic (no CLI dependencies)
- `src/main.rs` - CLI wrapper (uses `clap` and `tokio`, only compiled with `cli` feature)

**Event Support:**
- `modify` → `notify::EventKind::Modify`
- `close_write` → `notify::EventKind::Access(AccessKind::Close(AccessMode::Write))`
- `create` → `notify::EventKind::Create`
- `remove` → `notify::EventKind::Remove`

**Signal Handling:**
- Listen for `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` to shutdown gracefully
- Clean exit for proper workflow cleanup

### 5. Update Workspace Dependencies

**Root `Cargo.toml` additions:**
```toml
[workspace]
members = [
    # ... existing members ...
    "packages/file_watcher",
]

[workspace.dependencies]
# Add exact version with patch number:
notify = "8.2.0"
```

**Important:** Use `notify = "8.2.0"` (exact version including patch) per project requirements.

### 6. Integrate with `stream-watcher.sh`

**Update `.github/scripts/stream-watcher.sh`:**

**Line 269:**
```bash
# Before
log "Using inotify to watch stream file: $STREAM_FILE"

# After
log "Using file watcher to watch stream file: $STREAM_FILE"
```

**Lines 282-284:**
```bash
# Before
log "Starting inotifywait for stream monitoring..."
inotifywait -q -m -e modify,close_write "$stream_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
local inotify_pid=$!
log "Stream inotifywait PID: $inotify_pid"

# After
log "Starting file watcher for stream monitoring..."
moosicbox-file-watcher -q -m -e modify,close_write "$stream_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
local watcher_pid=$!
log "Stream file-watcher PID: $watcher_pid"
```

**Line 287:**
```bash
# Update variable reference
while kill -0 $watcher_pid 2>/dev/null; do
```

**Line 314:**
```bash
# Before
log "inotifywait process ended, finishing up..."

# After
log "file-watcher process ended, finishing up..."
```

### 7. Update GitHub Workflows

**Files to update:**
- `.github/workflows/claude-pr.yml`
- `.github/workflows/claude-issue.yml`

**Replace system package installation with Rust binary:**

**REMOVE:**
```yaml
# claude-pr.yml line 224-225
# claude-issue.yml line 109-110
- name: Install inotify-tools
  run: sudo apt-get install -y inotify-tools
```

**ADD** (after Rust toolchain setup, before "Start stream watcher"):
```yaml
- name: Setup file watcher
  uses: BSteffaniak/cache-artifact@master
  with:
    command: cargo build -p moosicbox_file_watcher --release --features cli
    shell: bash
    output-path: target/release/moosicbox-file-watcher
    artifact-name: moosicbox-file-watcher-ubuntu-latest-binary
    cache-key-prefix: file-watcher-claude
    make-executable: true
    verify-command: --version

- name: Add file watcher to PATH
  run: echo "${{ github.workspace }}/target/release" >> $GITHUB_PATH
```

**Note:** Include `--features cli` to build the binary with CLI dependencies.

## Verification Checklist

Before completing this issue, verify:

- [ ] Package builds successfully: `cargo build -p moosicbox_file_watcher --release --features cli`
- [ ] Library builds without CLI features: `cargo build -p moosicbox_file_watcher --release`
- [ ] Binary runs with `--version` and `--help`
- [ ] Clippy passes: `cargo clippy -p moosicbox_file_watcher --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] Format check passes: `cargo fmt -p moosicbox_file_watcher --check`
- [ ] Local testing: Binary can watch a directory and detect file changes
- [ ] Integration test: `stream-watcher.sh` works with new binary locally
- [ ] Workflow test: Changes work in CI on test branch
- [ ] `cargo-machete` passes: No unused dependencies
- [ ] `taplo format` passes for TOML files
- [ ] CLI dependencies are properly gated behind `cli` feature

## Testing Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Build with CLI feature
cargo build -p moosicbox_file_watcher --release --features cli

# Test watching a directory
target/release/moosicbox-file-watcher -m /tmp/test-dir &
WATCHER_PID=$!

# Trigger changes
echo "test" >> /tmp/test-dir/file.txt

# Verify watcher is alive
kill -0 $WATCHER_PID && echo "Watcher running"

# Cleanup
kill $WATCHER_PID
```

**Feature Testing:**
```bash
# Verify library builds without CLI deps
cargo build -p moosicbox_file_watcher --release --no-default-features

# Verify CLI binary requires the feature
cargo build -p moosicbox_file_watcher --release --bin moosicbox-file-watcher
# Should fail without --features cli
```

**Integration Testing:**
1. Test modified `stream-watcher.sh` locally with the new binary
2. Create test PR/issue to verify workflow changes work in CI
3. Verify GitHub comment updates work as expected

## Implementation Steps

1. ✅ Create package structure and implement core library
2. ✅ Add CLI binary with optional feature gating (following `openport` pattern)
3. ✅ Add to workspace and update dependencies
4. ✅ Add comprehensive tests for file watching functionality
5. ✅ Test locally with `stream-watcher.sh`
6. ✅ Update workflows with file watcher setup
7. ✅ Test in CI on feature branch
8. ✅ Update `stream-watcher.sh` to use new binary
9. ✅ Merge to main

## References

- `notify` crate: https://github.com/notify-rs/notify
- Optional dependency pattern: `packages/openport/Cargo.toml:19-31`
- Integration points: 
  - `.github/workflows/claude-pr.yml:224`
  - `.github/workflows/claude-issue.yml:109`
  - `.github/scripts/stream-watcher.sh:282`
- MoosicBox code style: `AGENTS.md`
- License compatibility: `deny.toml:97` (CC0-1.0 already approved)

items.title: Cache the dev image's dependency layers and stop baking node_modules

milestone.title: C2 · Dev environment & DevEx
milestone.description: .devcontainer/Codespaces + TypeScript. Closes: GitHub Codespaces, Developer Experience (DevEx), CLI, TypeScript, JavaScript, Node.js.

items.body:
## What problem does this solve?

The dev image (`containers/site/Dockerfile`) is slow to rebuild and carries far more than it serves.

- A `--no-cache` rebuild — the one that runs whenever `package-lock.json` or `requirements.txt` moves — took **2m02s** and re-downloaded every npm and pip artifact, because nothing was cached between builds.
- The `js` stage installs **121 npm packages (65 MB)** so the site can serve **five files** from them, and that tree is committed as a layer and copied into the final image, which weighed **565 MB**.
- The `pip install` layer sat *below* the `node_modules` copy, so an npm bump also reinstalled all of Python.

None of this is user-visible, but it is the loop that every dependency bump and every Dockerfile edit pays for.

## Proposed solution

1. Cache the installs with buildah `--mount=type=cache`: `/root/.npm` for `npm ci`, `/root/.cache/pip` for `pip install` (drop `--no-cache-dir`; a mount never enters a layer). Cache the apt `.deb` payload but not the index — reusing the index would mean no longer deleting the lists, which `DL3009` exists to prevent, so `DL3008` stays the only inline exception.
2. Move `requirements.txt` / `pip install` **above** the `node_modules` copy.
3. `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`; `pip install --no-compile` (the image already sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`) plus `PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1`.
4. Re-introduce `scripts/vendor.json` as the **single** source→destination map, read by both `scripts/mkdocs_vendor.py` and the image's `js` stage. The stage copies the five bundles out of `node_modules` and deletes the tree **inside the same `RUN`**, so the 121-package install is never committed; a separate prune step would leave the tree in the layer below.
5. Add `scripts/vendor.json` to `build.yml`'s `SITE_PATHS`, and change `Dockerfile.dockerignore` from `scripts/` to `scripts/*` + `!scripts/vendor.json` — dockerignore cannot re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded.

**Results, measured on this host:** `podman build --no-cache` **2m02s → 1m35s** (user CPU 70s → 43s); image **565 MB → 316 MB**; the five bundles are SHA-256 identical to a fresh `npm ci`; `scripts/dev.sh build` + `restart` gives `health=healthy` with all five assets serving 200.

## Alternatives considered

- **`[engine] tmp_dir` in `containers.conf`** to relocate the build cache: tested through `CONTAINERS_CONF` on both `podman build` and `buildah build` — it does not apply to `RUN --mount=type=cache`, which follows `TMPDIR` only.
- **Pointing `TMPDIR` at `/srv/myinfra/cache`** (the lab's `@cache` subvolume): it works, but the choice was to keep buildah's default `/var/tmp` (`nosuid,nodev,noexec`), so no host-specific path enters the Dockerfile.
- **Native overlay instead of `fuse-overlayfs`**: a storage config without `mount_program` built the same image in 1m51s — no gain, so no `storage.conf` change.
- **Keeping `vendor.json` deleted and duplicating the paths in the Dockerfile**: rejected — that is exactly the drift #252 removed.
- **`uv` instead of `pip`**: faster in isolation, but it adds a toolchain to a dev image for one step.
- **Not pruning `node_modules`**: leaves 249 MB of unused dependencies in the image plus ~5s of layer commit.

## Type

CI / tooling

## Scope

- [x] Infra / tooling (workflows, terraform, scripts)

No page, translation, `mkdocs.yml` or Terraform change, and no environment value is introduced.

## Checklist

- [x] `podman build --no-cache` clean; hadolint v2.15.1 at `--failure-threshold warning` clean
- [x] ruff and actionlint clean; `scripts/vendor.json` valid JSON
- [x] `scripts/dev.sh build` + `restart` → `health=healthy`; all five bundles serve 200
- [x] Bundles byte-identical to `npm ci` (SHA-256)
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md`, `containers/site/README.md` and `scripts/README.md` updated

items.title: Docker container fails to start Shiny app (visNetwork missing & permission issues)
items.body:
# Issue Report: Docker container fails to start Shiny app (`visNetwork` missing & permission issues)

### Describe the bug

I've been trying to self-host the web-app of prisma-flowdiagram and I encountered some issues when launching the docker container. The container successfully builds. But the launching command displays some error messages related to missing 'visNetwork' package & denied cache permissions.

When following the Docker installation instructions in `README.md` (`docker build . -t prisma-shiny:1` and `docker run -it --rm -p 3838:3838 prisma-shiny:1`), visiting `http://localhost:3838/app/` shows the following text:

```text
An error has occurred
The application failed to start.
The application exited during initialization.
```

Checking `/var/log/shiny-server/*.log` reveals two issues:

1. **Fatal Startup Error**: R halts because `visNetwork` is missing:
   ```text
   Error in loadNamespace(i, c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[i]]) : 
     there is no package called ‘visNetwork’
   Calls: runApp ... loadNamespace -> withRestarts -> withOneRestart -> doWithOneRestart
   Execution halted
   ```

2. **Permission Warning (`bslib` Sass cache)**:
   ```text
   Warning in dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE) :
     cannot create dir '/srv/shiny-server/prisma/app/app_cache', reason 'Permission denied'
   Warning in value[[3L]](cond) :
     Error using cache directory at '/srv/shiny-server/prisma/app/app_cache/sass'. Using temp dir instead.
   ```

### Root Cause Analysis

1. **Missing `visNetwork` runtime dependency**:
   - `PRISMA2020` depends on `DiagrammeR`, which directly imports `visNetwork` (`visNetwork (>= 2.1.0)`).
   - In the `Dockerfile`, `install.packages()` did not explicitly include `visNetwork`.
   - By default in R, `getOption("timeout")` is `60` seconds. On slower or fluctuating internet connections, downloading packages like `visNetwork` (4.4 MB) or `igraph` (5.0 MB) from Posit Package Manager / CRAN can exceed 60 seconds. When a download times out, `install.packages()` only emits a warning (`Warning: download of package '...' failed`) and still exits with status `0`. As a result, `docker build` completes without failing, creating a broken cached image with missing dependencies.

2. **Unnecessary `devtools` in `Dockerfile`**:
   - `devtools` was included in the `install.packages()` list in `Dockerfile`, dragging in over 60 dependencies (`pak`, `pkgbuild`, `pkgdown`, `roxygen2`, `testthat`, `usethis`, etc.) that are never used at runtime. This heavily inflated build times and increased download failure risks.

3. **File permissions on `/srv/shiny-server/prisma`**:
   - `shiny-server.conf` specifies `run_as shiny;`.
   - The files copied into `/srv/shiny-server/prisma/` are owned by `root:root` with default permissions (`drwxr-xr-x`). When `bslib` tries to write its Sass cache to `/srv/shiny-server/prisma/app/app_cache`, it throws `Permission denied`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Build the Docker image according to the README:
   ```bash
   docker build . -t prisma-shiny:1
   ```
2. Run the container:
   ```bash
   docker run -it --rm -p 3838:3838 prisma-shiny:1
   ```
3. In a web browser, navigate to:
   ```
   http://localhost:3838/app/
   ```
4. Observe the error page and check the logs inside the container:
   ```bash
   docker exec -it <container_id> cat /var/log/shiny-server/*.log
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The Shiny app should start without errors, compile assets cleanly into its cache, and display the PRISMA 2020 Flow Diagram user interface at `http://localhost:3838/app/`, even on slow internet connections.

### Proposed Fix

Modify `Dockerfile` to:
1. Increase R's download timeout (`options(timeout = 600)`) and add explicit installation of `visNetwork` along with other runtime dependencies (`bslib`, `dplyr`, `rmarkdown`, `progress`).
2. Remove unused `devtools`.
3. Add a post-installation validation check in R so `docker build` fails immediately if any package fails to install.
4. Set ownership of `/srv/shiny-server/prisma` to user `shiny` (`chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/prisma`).

#### Diff:

```diff
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -21,7 +21,12 @@ RUN apt-get update -qq && \
         pandoc
 
 # Install R packages
-RUN Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("DiagrammeR", "DiagrammeRsvg", "htmltools", "htmlwidgets", "scales", "shiny", "shinyjs", "stringr", "xml2", "DT", "rio", "zip", "rsvg", "webp", "devtools"))'
+RUN Rscript -e '\
+    options(timeout = 600); \
+    pkgs <- c("DiagrammeR", "DiagrammeRsvg", "htmltools", "htmlwidgets", "scales", "shiny", "shinyjs", "stringr", "xml2", "DT", "rio", "zip", "rsvg", "webp", "visNetwork", "bslib", "dplyr", "rmarkdown", "progress"); \
+    install.packages(pkgs); \
+    missing <- pkgs[!pkgs %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"]]; \
+    if (length(missing) > 0) stop("Failed to install: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))'
 
 # Copy the shiny server configuration
 COPY shiny-server.conf /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
@@ -34,6 +39,7 @@ RUN R CMD INSTALL /tmp/app
 RUN mkdir -p /srv/shiny-server/prisma/app && \
     echo "OK" > /srv/shiny-server/prisma/healthz.txt
 COPY inst/shiny-examples/PRISMA_flowdiagram/. /srv/shiny-server/prisma/app/
+RUN chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/prisma
 
 # Clean up downloaded files
 RUN rm -rf /tmp/*/downloaded_packages /tmp/app
```

### Environment

- **Base Docker Image**: `rocker/shiny:latest` (Ubuntu 24.04 noble, R 4.4+)
- **PRISMA2020 Version**: `1.1.5`
- **Host OS**: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- **Docker Version**: `29.9.0`

items.title: infra: enable unattended-upgrades for automatic security updates on the Hetzner VPS
items.body:
**Summary:** Add unattended-upgrades to `infra/harden.sh` for automatic security-only patching, with a fixed 04:00 UTC auto-reboot window for kernel updates.

## Plan

Add an idempotent unattended-upgrades section to `infra/harden.sh` (following the existing check-before-install + heredoc-overwrite pattern used by the fail2ban/ufw/sshd blocks), inserted after the `ufw` block and before the sshd-hardening block. Writes `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50unattended-upgrades` (explicit security-only `Allowed-Origins`, `Remove-Unused-Kernel-Packages`/`Remove-Unused-Dependencies` "true", `Automatic-Reboot` "true" at a fixed `04:00` UTC window) and `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades` (enables the periodic timer), then `systemctl enable --now unattended-upgrades`.

Reboot policy decided with the user: **automatic reboot at a fixed 04:00 UTC time** (not silent-anytime, not notify-only — this is a single-instance personal box with no notification channel wired up, so notify-only wouldn't be actionable in practice).

Also updates `infra/README.md`'s provisioning description and its `## Verify` section with unattended-upgrades checks. No new Tofu resource is needed — `main.tf`'s `null_resource.harden` already re-runs `harden.sh` on any content change via its `filesha256` trigger.

Per `CLAUDE.md`'s Tooling/harness carve-out (scripts are explicitly excluded from auto-merge), this PR will **not** use auto-merge — it stays open for manual review, since `harden.sh` runs as root against the live production VPS.

OS release upgrades (e.g. 24.04→26.04) are explicitly out of scope for this issue — tracked separately in a follow-up issue.

---

**Summary:** The Hetzner VPS provisioned in #1030 has no automatic security-patch mechanism — `apt` packages (including the kernel, OpenSSH, and Docker) only get updated if someone SSHes in and runs `apt upgrade` by hand. For a single-admin personal box, unpatched CVEs can sit indefinitely.

## Suggested approach
- Add `unattended-upgrades` (Ubuntu's standard mechanism, already in the default repos — no new dependency) to `infra/harden.sh`, configured for security-only updates plus a scheduled reboot window if a kernel update needs one (`/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50unattended-upgrades` + `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades`).
- Idempotent, same pattern as the rest of `harden.sh` — re-running `tofu apply` should pick this up automatically via the script's `triggers` hash, no manual SSH step needed.
- Decide: silent reboots on kernel updates (simplest, brief downtime on a single-instance app) vs. notify-only (no auto-downtime, but patches don't fully land without a manual reboot) — worth a quick decision before implementing, given this is a single always-on personal app.

Sub-issue of #1029's Hetzner migration (parallel track to #1030's hardening, not blocking it).

items.body:
I installed PCL by `sudo apt install libpcl-dev`. and used it like this:
```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.5)
project(test)

# Default to C99
if(NOT CMAKE_C_STANDARD)
  set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 99)
endif()

# Default to C++14
